edit.description: the mount-dead re-read's cases, every one of which sets the mount before the run and never moves it

summary: the mount-dead re-read's cases move the mount between the child's exit and the read — the transition all five of them claim and none exercises

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

acceptance: the re-read's cases exercise a mount that changed in the gap: a chain that broke after an earlier re-read of the same run read it clean still ends the run, and a committed repair of a queue that was unparseable at the child's exit still declines the abort — so a supervisor answering from its own first resolve rather than from the tip reds on the first and a supervisor blind to the repair reds on the second; the five standing cases keep their static mounts and no `src/` change
pins: a mount-dead re-read ends the run on a chain that broke after an earlier re-read read it clean
a mount-dead re-read declines the abort on a queue repaired between the child's exit and the read
notes: Measured here: all five cases under `a mount-dead 69 aborts only while the mount is still dead` set disk before `runOver69` and never move it, so a memoized `resolveChain` (`src/loopSupervisor.ts:528`) passes every one, and the clean case asserts the `has been repaired since` warn over a mount nothing repaired. The property holds (repeated `tsImport` re-reads entry and deps), hence pins. The re-read resolves the tip, so a gap repair commits; `:3627` already mutates disk inside `runTick`.
